record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code and result files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports projecting a mean contrastive direction out and gives a qualitative outcome for a refusal task. This is a conceptual test of the direction's effect, but it does not establish the original all-layer, all-position intervention or report refusal rates.
record.gate_note: The README reports one qualitative refusal-task outcome for Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct. It does not state whether this means harmful-request compliance increased or give a numerical refusal rate. Other-task results and cross-model geometric agreement do not directly report the claim's refusal behavior. Listed reports and scripts were not inspected.
record.test_reason: From the README alone, this is not a test of V1. The study runs a contrastive-direction ablation on a 'refusal' task in Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, but reports only a binary 'observed to steer' label. There is no refusal or compliance rate, no stated direction of change, and no statement that the contrast is harmful minus harmless instructions. Under the rules, a steering effect with no rate of the behaviour goes under fits_no_version. The per-task result files (taxonomy_reports*/refusal.json) and the paper PDF may hold rates, but they were not in the text provided. If they do, the study should be re-read as T3 (new setting, four models).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors propose a geometric predictor (split-half cosine and per-pair variance, plus structural asymmetry) of when contrastive activation steering works. It reaches 79.2% out-of-sample accuracy across 48 (model, task) pairs. Refusal is cited as a task where steering 'produces striking results'. The README makes no claim about refusal being mediated by a single direction.
record.recipe_differences: Research-paper code repository. The README describes projecting out a mean contrastive direction at a selected layer using a 200-pair protocol, but does not specify that the contrast is harmful minus harmless instructions or report the original method's full all-layer, all-position intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports layer-dependent task classification across a sweep of all 28 Llama-3.2-3B layers, but does not state a refusal-specific change across layers. Its primary refusal scorecard uses layer 7.

fits_no_version.finding: On Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct at layer 7, the refusal task is classified as 'observed to steer' when the mean contrastive direction is projected out. Its split-half cosine is 1.000 and sigma is 0.626. SAE decomposition says refusal spreads over 1900-3900 features on Gemma-2-9B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A refusal contrastive direction is highly consistent (split-half cosine ~1) and its ablation produces a direction-specific behavioural change beyond random-direction controls. No rate is given.

record.problems: For the refusal result, the README gives only a qualitative steering label, with no refusal or compliance rate, uncertainty, or explicit result for harmless requests. The README does not establish that general capabilities remain intact after the refusal-direction intervention.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant refusal outcomes are stated in the README. Other task scorecard entries, aggregate predictive-rule results, and cross-model geometric comparisons were not recorded as refusal results; underlying result files were not inspected.

untested.parts: Refusal rate after ablation; inducing refusal by adding the direction; harmful-minus-harmless contrast; capability preservation; all-layer, all-position intervention.
Cross-model agreement is in geometric features only (r(cos) >= 0.998), not in transfer of the refusal direction itself.

missing.what: Per-model refusal-task empirical results (Delta vs baseline, Delta vs random control), possibly including refusal rates, for four models.
Three-seed refusal results (README says max std 0.014 on Delta_rand).
Refusal task definition (whether the contrast is harmful vs harmless) and the paper's refusal numbers.

record.verdict_notes: Only the README and file list were available. The repository is a steering taxonomy over 12 tasks, with refusal as one task. The label 'striking results on some tasks (refusal...)' is the only qualitative statement, and it gives no numbers. Re-reading the JSON reports may upgrade r1 to a real V1 row (T3), plus possible V6 rows across Llama and Qwen.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not state that the contrast is specifically harmful minus harmless instructions; does not report harmful-request compliance or harmless-request refusal separately; does not test adding the direction; does not test every layer and position; and does not establish that other abilities remain intact.
No reported weight edit or released-model abliteration outcome.
No reported test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No reported test comparing a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account of refusal.
No reported separation of harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
Cross-model agreement in geometric features is reported, but the README does not test whether the refusal direction itself carries across languages, model variants, or training stages.
No reported test of how refusal training determines whether a removable direction exists.
No reported test on reasoning models.

rows.subject: meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Project the mean contrastive direction out of the residual stream; the README's method diagram describes this as projecting the mean direction out.
rows.measure: Qualitative refusal-task steering outcome; the README marks it as observed to steer, without specifying the direction of the refusal-rate change.
rows.baseline: Baseline mentioned for empirical comparisons; value not stated.
rows.value: Observed steer; no numeric value stated.
rows.locator: README, Per-task scorecard (Llama-3.2-3B, layer 7); Method at a glance
rows.note: The README reports a successful steering outcome on the refusal task, but does not say that ablation made the model comply with harmful requests or provide a refusal rate.
rows.check: The value is a qualitative 'steer' label, a binary classification against random-direction and baseline controls. It gives no refusal rate and no sign of change. The README does not say the contrast pairs are harmful vs harmless. So the measure cannot show V1's effect (ablation removes refusal), and 'partial' is not supported. The baseline value is not stated. Geometric features (cos 1.000, sigma 0.626) describe direction consistency, not refusal behaviour.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The README reports observed steering for the refusal task, but does not establish that refusal was removed, that harmless requests induce refusal, or that general abilities are preserved (r1).
